title: How Casey Adams went from a neck injury to founding MediaKits: momentum, commitment, and timing
summary: Casey Adams traces his path from a high school sports injury to podcasting, a book, and co-founding MediaKits, a creator analytics tool. He stresses stacking small wins, going all in on a venture, spotting problems firsthand, and building confidence through uncomfortable repetition.

principles.text: Stack small early wins; they build momentum that keeps you committed longer.
principles.quote: just micro wins do build momentum and i believe momentum helps you stick with something longer and have more fulfillment in the process

principles.text: Once you have something worth pursuing, go all in; part-time founding invites hurdles.
principles.quote: there's no part-time founder and if you are a part-time founder it's i'm sure you're gonna have a lot of hurdles

principles.text: Don't wait for perfect timing; the right moment never just arrives.
principles.quote: if you have a great idea and you know you don't think the time is right like the truth is the time will never just be right

principles.text: Turn a non-technical weakness into a strength by making team-building your core focus.
principles.quote: we're non-technical co-founders right which could be looked at as a disadvantage but for us we use it to our advantage to build an incredible team and to make that our core focus

principles.text: Build products from problems you see firsthand, like repeatedly hand-editing a friend's outdated media kit.
principles.quote: why isn't there a way for creators to easily share their data and analytics that never get outdated that you can simply share through a link

principles.text: Build confidence by putting yourself out there and introducing yourself to people.
principles.quote: to build confidence number one is like put yourself out there and just introduce yourself to people and start learning more about them
